summary: After a layoff a plant keeps producing about as much per worker as before, so the employer does not necessarily pay for it in output.
realLife: An NBER plant-level study found layoffs had no measurable effect on the productivity of the workers who stayed, and suggested seniority rules and heavy reliance on equipment as reasons.
sources: NBER working paper w1807, The Economic Performance of Survivors after Layoffs: https://www.nber.org/papers/w1807
inGame: employer's output per worker read from job records after job-ended events.

turns.summary: A small shop loses its best person and output drops.
turns.writesBack: employer output lower; boss mood: worried

turns.summary: Output holds but the room goes quiet.

pulledBy: a former worker on good terms
